column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated [his request] several times, and he said: “Do not become angry.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.

The ḥāfiẓ [Ibn Ḥajar] said in al-Fatḥ (10/520): “Al-Khaṭṭābī said: The meaning of his words, ‘Do not become angry’, is: avoid the causes of anger and do not expose yourself to what brings it on. As for anger itself, it cannot be forbidden,

because it is something natural that cannot be removed from one's make-up.” He also said: “Ibn al-Tīn said: In his words, ‘Do not become angry’, he ﷺ combined the good of this world and the Hereafter,
because anger leads to cutting ties and to withholding gentleness, and it may lead to harming the one at whom one is angry, which detracts from one's religion.”
Allah has praised those who restrain their anger and pardon people, and the Prophet ﷺ informed us that “the strong one is not the one who overpowers others in wrestling;

the strong one is only the one who controls himself when angry.” Reported by al-Bukhārī (6114). When a person becomes angry, he should restrain his anger and seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil,
as in al-Bukhārī (6115); and he should sit or lie down, as in Sunan Abī Dāwūd (4782), where Abū Dharr reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down; if the anger leaves him [well and good], otherwise let him lie down.” It is an authentic hadith whose narrators are narrators of Muslim.
shown by this Companion's asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for advice.
A warning against the causes of anger and the consequences that follow from it.
The repetition of the advice against anger, which shows how important that advice is.
